items.title: Frankie Valli Denies News Reports He Has Retired; Brother Apologizes for Claiming He Was Done, Saying ‘I Was Misinformed’
items.summary:
Frankie Valli says he has not retired. The 92-year-old singer posted a brief statement to his social accounts on Friday afternoon reading, "In spite of what you might have heard, I am not retired. Frankie," pushing back on several days of news reports that his career had ended.

Those reports traced back to a Facebook post from Valli's younger brother, Bobby Valli, published Wednesday, which said in part, "He will now retire. We will always have special memories of Frankie Valli. He has reached a place in his life where his family is there to love, cherish and to be there for him." By Friday afternoon Bobby Valli had edited the post to remove the retirement claim and issued an apology of his own: "I apologize. I was misinformed. I was under the impression my brother Frankie was retiring. Hoping for him to have a speedy recovery to continue his illustrious career!"

Valli's longtime representative, Victoria Varela, told Variety earlier Friday, "He is not retired. This is false," after another outlet ran a headline announcing his retirement from performing after 60 years onstage. Valli has in fact been performing for 75 years.

The confusion grew out of a real health situation. On May 31, Valli canceled the remaining dates of his farewell tour, The Last Encores, writing that he had "decided to take the rest of the year off from touring to focus on my health." Varela said at the time that the shows were canceled rather than postponed so ticket buyers would get refunds instead of having their money held while he recovered: "Promoters want to prolong things and not give people their money back," she said, "but he realized he needed to take a break and get his health in order."

Valli's last concert was Feb. 22 at Pechanga Resort Casino in Temecula. He rose to fame fronting the Four Seasons in the 1960s on hits including "Walk Like a Man," "Big Girls Don't Cry," "Rag Doll" and "Can't Take My Eyes Off You," entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1990 and received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2026. His story became the Broadway musical Jersey Boys, which ran from 2005 to 2017 and was adapted for film by Clint Eastwood in 2014.

items.title: Courtney Love Reveals She ‘Almost Died’ in 2019 Amid Mystery Illness
items.summary:
Courtney Love says she nearly died in 2019 from an illness she has never fully detailed publicly. In a video posted to Instagram, the musician described her body "just exploded" after she moved from Los Angeles to London that year, leading to repeated hospital stays. "I almost died," she said. "I lost all my hair. I was about 100 pounds. And they told me I was going to die. I didn't believe them."

Love framed the video, reported on by Rolling Stone, as a goodbye before stepping away from social media to do what she called "analog stuff for a few weeks." She also answered the question she says fans keep asking about her long-awaited solo album. "It's done. It's kind of been done," she said. "It's a really good record. I put a lot into it."

She connected her refusal to accept the prognosis to childhood memories of adults contradicting what she could plainly see. "They'd say red was blue, and then I'd see blue," she said, describing how she would gaslight herself into wondering whether they were right. "I never really lost my ability to see that fucking red was red, despite them telling me that red was blue. And so when they said I was going to die, I just didn't believe them. And somehow I got better. I'm healthy, which is amazing."

Love was blunt about the commercial failure of Hole's last album, 2010's Nobody's Daughter, calling the experience "spectacularly humbling" and citing a festival slot at Pizza Hut Park at 11 a.m. beneath Limp Bizkit and 30 Seconds to Mars. She was warmer about the current landscape: "People sound great live," she said. "The girlies are amazing. Shit's amazing. I just need to like, understand how to do this. I will be back."

The album, according to her Instagram caption, features collaborators including Green Day's Billie Joe Armstrong and her longtime friend Michael Stipe. "I want to tour more than anything, and I want to sing," she wrote. "That's what keeps my soul and body happy." Love was also the subject of Antiheroine, a documentary from directors Edward Lovelace and James Hall that premiered at Sundance in January. A Hole reunion is not in the works.

items.title: Slipknot Confirm Sid Wilson Fired After 28 Years
items.summary:
Slipknot have confirmed that Sid Wilson, the turntablist known as #0 and an original member of the band, is out after 28 years. A graphic posted to the group's social accounts read, "Effective immediately, Slipknot will no longer be associated with Sid Wilson. We wish him the best in his future endeavors." The posts came down roughly ten minutes later, which is how the band has handled other recent lineup announcements.

The confirmation follows a TMZ report two weeks earlier that Wilson had been permanently removed from the group, a decision the outlet attributed to the band having had enough of how he treated his bandmates. Stereogum noted that neither Slipknot nor Wilson responded publicly at the time, though guitarist Jim Root, #4, posted, "Don't believe everything you read."

Wilson also performs with his own band SID and as a solo artist under the name DJ Starscream. His exit continues a run of departures from the Iowa group's ranks, following original percussionist Chris Fehn (#3), original keyboardist Craig Jones (#5) and longtime drummer Jay Weinberg.

Kelly Osbourne, who has a child with Wilson and recently called off their engagement, posted a series of Instagram stories after the initial report. "Wake the fuck up take some responsibility I will not take your shit anymore," she wrote. "I want to be happy and I have a beautiful son to raise. Leave me alone. let me heal. I can't protect you from yourself anymore." In another story she added, "Also while I'm at it can I have my dogs back and all my possessions. Oh yeah and maybe some child support?"

Slipknot's most recent live performance was at Inkcarceration 2025. The band has not named a replacement for Wilson.

items.title: ‘Frozen 3’ “Royal Wedding” Between Anna and Kristoff Is Crashed by New Villain in First-Look
items.summary:
Disney showed the first footage from Frozen 3 at its D23 fan event on Friday, revealing that the film builds toward a royal wedding between Anna and Kristoff — and that a new villain interrupts it. The third entry in the animated franchise opens in theaters on Nov. 24, 2027.

Idina Menzel and Kristen Bell walked onstage hand in hand and performed a rendition of "Frozen Heart" that ran into some technical trouble, with Bell teasing that Anna and Elsa are heading out on their biggest journey yet. The pair confirmed the wedding, saying it had been a long time coming, and added that love is in the air for everyone, Olaf included. Josh Gad then appeared to sing a love song to Samantha, a callback to a running joke from Frozen II.

Menzel introduced the footage by declaring, "We will find ourselves far from Arendelle in wild and dangerous land." According to The Hollywood Reporter, the clip showed the wedding apparently being crashed, with Anna and Kristoff trudging through an icy forest as the villain descends from a snowy peak and says, "The sisters of Arrendale, we finally meet."

The stakes are considerable. The 2013 original grossed $1.28 billion worldwide and 2019's Frozen II took in $1.45 billion. Menzel and Bell return as Elsa and Anna, with Gad as Olaf and Jonathan Groff as Kristoff.

Frozen 3 originally carried a 2026 release date before Disney moved it. Gad explained the delay in 2025: "There's a reason the movie is coming out in 2027 and that is because no one wants to rush this. Everyone wants this to not just be a sequel or a money grab. They want this to be absolutely worthy of the story we set out to make in 2013." Former Disney CEO Bob Iger has also said a Frozen 4 is in development, though the studio has not scheduled it.

items.title: Locarno Film Festival Winners: Florin Șerban, Monica Bellucci & Hong Sangsoo Among Victors
items.summary:
Florin Șerban's You Don't Belong Here (Nu E Locul Tau Aici) won the Pardo d'Oro at the 79th Locarno Film Festival, the top prize carrying CHF 75,000 split between director and producer. The Romanian drama marks Șerban's return to features after eight years, and the international competition jury cited "the strength of its writing, the singularity of its vision, and its exceptional command of cinematic language."

The film follows a physician whose life comes apart when police suspect his teenage son of murdering an elderly Romani man, and who then learns his son has been vandalizing cars alongside masked vigilantes. Teodor Butănescu received a special mention for his performance in the film.

Elsewhere in the main competition, Matheus Farias and Enock Carvalho took the Special Jury Prize for the Brazilian-German The Riverbank (A Margem do Rio), while Hong Sangsoo won the Pardo for Best Direction for Nowhere to Lay My Eyes (Nun Dul Dega Eomne). The two Best Performance awards went to Kim Minhee for the Hong film and Monica Bellucci for Giovanni Tortorici's Kettic. Alessandra Sanguinetti's The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer swept both the Pardo d'Oro in the Concorso Cineasti del Presente and the Swatch First Feature Award.

Festival artistic director Giona A. Nazzaro called the results "a vital and contemporary slate of awards, in close dialogue with the transformations in the industry and in our world today," saying the jury "upheld the primacy of form and of language" while remaining accessible in its choices. Belgian filmmaker Fabrice Du Welz presided over the international competition jury, joined by producer Marco Alessi and actors Lolita Chammah and Paulina García, along with ARTE France Cinéma's Olivier Père.

As Deadline reported, the festival closes Saturday, Aug. 15, in the Piazza Grande with the Prix du Public UBS ceremony followed by a screening of Marc Fitoussi's Ni Vue, Ni Connue (All About Corinne), starring Isabelle Huppert and Sandrine Kiberlain. Locarno's 80th edition is scheduled for Aug. 4 to 14, 2027.
